messages:
maria: quick ping — can someone take a look at PR #8532? it tweaks streaming chunk flush (5ms -> 1ms) and adds an X-Tool-Call header for tool routing. tests pass locally but go client CI is flaky. https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8532
jon: on it — what flakes are you seeing? any stack or log snippet?
maria: intermittent panic in go-client stream reader: 'invalid header format' when parsing headers on very short chunks. my hunch: header boundary can get split across frames after the faster flush.
aaron: can you paste the failing log?
maria: sure, pasted from CI below:
```
panic: invalid header format
  runtime.throw({0xabcdef, 0x12345})
  /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:1116 +0x72
net/http: invalid header field value
github.com/redwood/infra/clients/go/stream.(*reader).parseHeader(0xc000...)
  /workspace/clients/go/stream/reader.go:142 +0x1a3
```
lina: looks like parseHeader assumes header arrives in one Read buffer. with 1ms flush we're seeing splits where header name and value end up in separate frames.
jon: simplest fix: allow incremental header parsing (accumulate until "

"). fallback: treat empty chunk/frame as keepalive and skip parsing. also add a test that forces header split across frames.
maria: pushed a change that accumulates partial headers and treats zero-length frames as keepalive. added unit test that simulates header splitting — PTAL @jon @aaron
ci-bot: CI update: go-client/unit-tests — 2 jobs running, 1 failed (stream/reader_test.go) — https://ci.internal/redwood/build/98765
aaron: I'll take a look tonight. if it looks good i'll approve; prefer to merge tomorrow AM to avoid pushing during EMEA on-call window. :thumbsup:
jon: I can review the parsing change first thing, thanks for adding the test.
maria: thanks all — ping me if you see anything weird in the test, i can iterate quickly. :heart:
